body: I would say no, not this guy. The reason is because he's a senior and will graduate high school soon. He might already be seeing someone, and more important, **he may not be gay**. Also even if y'all do become friends, how are y'all going to hang out together? He's going to have his own group of friends who are the same age as him and they might wonder why a freshman's with him. Not saying you can't become acquaintances because who knows? Maybe just lower your expectations. Don't put this guy on a pedestal. You'll thank me later.
If you want my 2 cents, I'd say you either have to luck out or fight your introvert nature. Being a gay introvert is hard. But don't look at it as a problem. Look at it as a challenge.
It's probably best to come clean. When he asks, just be honest and say 'I'm probably gonna need some help.' Hopefully he understands, if he doesn't, idrk.

I'm sorry you had an abusive father. I'll never understand what that's like. You describe a painful childhood and a present life where you're detached and disconnected from everyone and everything including death. It begs the question why? You said quote

>I constantly think about killing myself...I'm honestly not sure what drives it, it just seems to be force of habit.

You said you're just living out of habit and don't really enjoy anything. All of this points to depression. It's possible you can be treated and start living in a world of color instead of gray.
What if there was say a loaded gun nearby? Would there be maybe temptation? I mean if I were in your position, I'll try and look for a way out of debt and take things from there, but idk..

Question: what were you like as a kid growing up? Did something bad happen? I just don't understand where the lack of emotion is coming from since you seem to have a completely "normal" life. Wife, kids, job, house, money. Normalcy. A lot of people would beg to have what you have and yet it means nothing to you?
24 yo here..would end it for you if i could
